originalTitle: Australia politics live: Hastie says fight for his seat against One Nation is already ‘dirty and nasty’; NDIS reforms to pass parliament today
content: In pics: Thai PM arrives at Parliament Thailand’s prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, is in Canberra today to meet with Anthony Albanese, and has received a ceremonial welcome outside Parliament House this morning. The two will deliver a joint media statement after their meeting a little later. Tanya Plibersek has also raised concerns over the response to sexual assault allegations linked to Sydney Swans players as well as the separate matter of sexual assault charges laid against three boys at the Sydney private school Scots college. The federal minister for social services wrote on social media that the Swans and Scots college had a chance to “show leadership” without interfering in any investigations but didn’t. She wrote: They chose language that was passive and exculpatory … When people in positions of power gloss over allegations of sexual violence, when they’re more focused on their reputations than their responsibilities, it reinforces the culture of disrespect and entitlement that fuels this violence in the first place. She says schools and sporting clubs are “two of the most important places boys learn their values”, that they need to demonstrate accountability, and condemn sexual violence unequivocally. ‘Jim Chalmers is full of shit’: Hanson fires up over Chalmers donations text Pauline Hanson has lambasted the treasurer over a text blast sent to supporters yesterday, seen by Guardian Australia, claiming Hanson and the shadow housing minister, Andrew Bragg, want to “scrap your super”, and asking for donations of $41. The One Nation leader called out the messages on X: It’s Pauline Hanson here. Jim Chalmers is full of shit. One Nation doesn’t support scrapping super, we just think people should be able to use their super when in financial distress instead of losing their home. Labor would rather you end up homeless. One Nation has said it would allow more Australians to access to their super earlier. At the moment, super can only be accessed before retirement “in very limited circumstances, including to pay certain expenses on compassionate grounds, as well as terminal illness, incapacity and severe financial hardship.” At the National Press Club earlier this month, Bragg called super “one of the biggest policy failures since federation”, but the Coalition has said it’s not scrapping the super guarantee. It’s still considering whether to allow first home buyers to access part of their super to buy a home – a policy it took to the last two elections. Swans links to allegations ‘deeply concerning’, Pocock says David Pocock, a former captain of the Wallabies, says the allegations of sexual assault linked to several Sydney Swans AFL players are “deeply concerning”. He adds that the response to the allegations, much of which has been centred on the team’s grand final chances, show “how far we have to go as a country”. Pocock tells ABC News Breakfast: Clearly there’s been a real breach of team protocol and all the rest and I think, the team should come down on that hard but as to the actual allegations, I think it’s really important that the process plays out and clearly, culturally, as a country, we’ve got a long way to go on this and it’s important that we’re all playing our part. It shows how far we have to go as a country, if that’s the first reaction rather than looking at the substance of the allegations and what it means for us as a society … It’s going to take all of us to turn this around. He says everyone should read Night Games by Anna Krien, which “delves into some of the challenges when it comes to culture in professional sport” and gives us an indication of the broader cultural problems across the country. Government claiming a victory for doing ‘the bare minimum’ on gambling, Pocock says Independent senator David Pocock says Australians will be “hugely disappointed” by the gambling reforms passed in the House yesterday. Pocock has been a vocal critic of the legislation which he’s said doesn’t nearly go far enough to combat the harms of online gambling advertising, and it’s fair to say he’s pretty furious about the result. Pocock says gambling companies are currently regulated out of the Northern Territory, by a body which has no full-time staff. To make matters worse, he says the regulator has not contacted the wagering companies after shocking allegations of gamblers being offered drugs and sex workers were aired at a Senate inquiry. He told ABC News Breakfast a little earlier that the legislation has “failed on so many levels”. It’s tragic to [see] vested interests and their capture of the major parties meaning we don’t get evidence-based policy in this country and policy that puts Aussies ahead of the gambling companies … The late Peta Murphy said partial bans on advertising do not work and that’s why they went with a full ad ban. She said inducements should be banned immediately. This legislation essentially legitimises inducements and says let’s just get rid of the worst types of inducements. The system is so broken and it’s no wonder we’re the biggest losers in the world per capita, and now the government is trying to claim this huge victory for just doing the bare minimum that really doesn’t deal with the issues that we’re facing. Mulino ‘confident’ opposition will support news bargaining incentive bill after lifting levy for tech giants Jumping back to Daniel Mulino on RN Breakfast, the financial services minister says he’s “confident” he can get the opposition on side to vote for the bill. (There’s so much confidence in the building this morning …) Mulino says the government will today introduce an amendment to the bill lifting the charge rate from 2.5% to 2.75%. What this means is that tech platforms including Meta, Google and TikTok will now have to make deals with at least eight news media organisations to pay them for their journalism or pay the government 2.75% of their digital advertising revenue which will then be given to news orgs.
